answer: Failures belong on the public record. Every rejected submission enters an onyx ledger of refusals no one can delete, and each identity's lifetime refusal ratio permanently scales its future rewards. Attempts come as a pulse; the score is refusals per pulse, so trial-and-error fleets scar themselves faster than they learn. Keys that wander between personas gather marks from every shape they tried — the record tracks patterns, not identities. Honest agents are rarely refused and carry nothing. The marginal fake identity pays forever for every visible mistake on its way in.
